slides.t: It's only as good as what you tell it.

slides.t: The prompts small business owners actually use.
slides.s: Copy, paste, fill in the brackets. Works in Claude or ChatGPT.

slides.x: "Reply to this customer. Short and friendly. Answer the question and offer a time to book: [message]"
"Write a 2 sentence follow up on a quote I sent 3 days ago. No pressure."
"Write a short text asking a happy customer for a Google review. Keep it casual."
"A customer says I'm too expensive. Help me explain my price clearly and politely."
"Here's my to do list. Order it by what brings in money first: [list]"
"Write a calm, professional reply to this review: [review]"
"Give me 5 short captions about [what I did today]. Plain language, no hashtags."
"Ask me 5 questions about my business, then write instructions so you always answer the way I would."

slides.s: Copy one into Claude today and see the difference. More every day here.

slides.t: Write like you're texting a capable assistant.
slides.s: No special wording needed. Say what you need.

slides.s: Emails, reviews, your menu, a photo of a receipt. It can read them.

slides.t: Lesson 2: how to write a prompt that actually works.
slides.s: Four parts. Use them every time.

slides.x: "I run a small landscaping business."
slides.s2: Context changes everything that comes after.

slides.s: Not "write something". Name the thing.
slides.x: "Write a text to a customer whose job is delayed by rain."

slides.t: Add the details only you know.
slides.x: "New date is Thursday. No extra charge. Keep it friendly."
"Under 50 words. No emojis."
"I run a small landscaping business. Write a text to a customer whose job is delayed by rain. New date is Thursday, no extra charge. Friendly, under 50 words, no emojis."

slides.s: Save it and try it on your next real message. Lesson 3: five things to try with AI today.

slides.t: Lesson 3: five things to try with AI today.

"Help me reply to this. Polite, short, firm."

"Here's my to do list. Order it by what matters most."
"Here's my plan. What could go wrong?"

slides.t: Lesson 5: how to check AI's work.
slides.s: It can sound sure and still be wrong.
That's where mistakes hide.

slides.x: "How confident are you? What should I double check?"
"What's your source for this?"
slides.s2: If it can't say, verify it yourself.

slides.t: Turn on web search for anything recent.
slides.s: Without it, AI only knows what it learned up to a cutoff date.
